description: We are a complete team from Kolkata working on an AI system.
summary: GeoLens is a web-based research tool that detects environmental change in West Bengal, India, from satellite imagery. A researcher uploads two satellite images of the same location, one historical and one recent, and a temporal convolutional neural network compares them to identify what changed. It classifies the change (normal, flood, wildfire, cyclone or landslide) and assigns a Low, Moderate or High risk level from the model’s confidence and a change score. Alongside the analysis tool, GeoLens monitors floods, droughts and vegetation across 15 locations in West Bengal, with location photo galleries and a curated local news desk for context. West Bengal faces monsoon floods in the Sundarbans and Malda, drought on the western laterite plateau, and loss of mangroves and forest. Satellite data on these changes exists, but comparing images over time is slow and needs specialist GIS tools. GeoLens makes that comparison fast and readable in the browser, so researchers can see what is changing, where, and how severe it is.
details:
What it does: GeoLens answers three of the challenge’s questions for a chosen location: what is changing, where, and how much. Researchers supply a historical and a recent satellite image (GeoTIFF) of one place. GeoLens returns a predicted change class and a risk level.

How it works:

  1. Preprocessing (Rasterio, NumPy): removes invalid pixels, clips each band to the 2nd–98th percentile, normalises both images together so they are comparable, and resizes to 256×256.
  2. Temporal CNN (PyTorch): one shared encoder turns each image into 512 features. The model compares the historical features, the recent features and their absolute difference (1,536 features in total).
  3. Output: one of five classes (Normal, Flood, Wildfire, Cyclone, Landslide), plus a Low, Moderate or High risk level derived from model confidence and the change score.

Data: The model was trained on NASA HLS Sentinel-2 (HLSS30) B08 near-infrared GeoTIFF imagery of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) region, spanning 2025 to September 2026. HLS is NASA’s harmonized surface reflectance product built from ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 observations.

Platform: monitoring pages for floods, droughts and vegetation across 15 West Bengal locations (5 per area), location photo galleries, a recent-news desk, and a researcher workspace for image-pair analysis.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (hosted on GitHub Pages), Python, PyTorch, Rasterio, NumPy.

Code: https://github.com/samantakoushik742-ux/GeoLens

Limitations: results support research and are not official disaster warnings. News is curated by our team. Coverage is currently limited to West Bengal.

Next steps: live Sentinel satellite feeds, saved analysis history for researchers, and expansion to more districts across India.
